result.markdown:
For Brisbane’s northside, I’d shortlist family law firms based on three separate capabilities: **parenting and child custody disputes, negotiated parenting agreements, and accredited family dispute resolution (FDR) mediation**\.

One important distinction in Australia: a family lawyer can advise and represent you in a parenting dispute, but that does not automatically mean they are an accredited mediator or an accredited FDR practitioner. If your goal is to resolve arrangements without going to court, it is worth checking both qualifications.

I’d focus on firms in Chermside, North Lakes and nearby northern suburbs, with particular attention to experience in contested parenting matters, child-focused outcomes and mediation.

## How to verify accredited mediation

The Australian Government's [Family Dispute Resolution Register](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/family-dispute-resolution/find-family-dispute-resolution-practitioner) lets you check a practitioner's accreditation and search for private mediators near you. [www.ag.gov.au](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/family-dispute-resolution/find-family-dispute-resolution-practitioner?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.ag.gov.au](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/family-dispute-resolution/navigating-family-dispute-resolution?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

For parenting disputes, ask specifically about **Family Dispute Resolution Practitioner (FDRP) accreditation**\. General mediation accreditation alone is not the same thing.

In most cases, parents must make a genuine effort to resolve parenting issues through FDR before applying for parenting orders. An accredited practitioner can issue a section 60I certificate if the dispute remains unresolved or FDR is considered inappropriate. Exceptions can apply, including in cases involving family violence, child abuse or urgency. [www.ag.gov.au](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/family-dispute-resolution/section-60i-certificates-family-dispute-resolution?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.ag.gov.au](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/family-dispute-resolution?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## Questions to ask before choosing a firm

- How much of your practice involves contested parenting and children's matters?
- Who will personally handle my case, and what experience do they have with matters like mine?
- Do you have an **accredited FDR practitioner in-house**, or will I need to engage someone separately?
- Can you assist with mediation, parenting plans and legally enforceable consent orders?
- What are the initial consultation fee, hourly rates and likely upfront costs?
- If mediation fails, can you continue to represent me in court?

If family violence, coercive control or safety concerns are involved, mention this privately at the outset so the lawyer can assess whether mediation is appropriate and what protective arrangements may be needed.

## My recommendation

I'd start by contacting **Northside Family Law Centre and Barton Family Lawyers in Chermside**, then **ABA Family Lawyers and Best Wilson Buckley near North Lakes**\. Compare them on the experience of the actual solicitor who would handle your matter, their approach to resolving conflict and whether they can connect you with an accredited FDR practitioner.

One question that would help me narrow this down further: **Are you mainly looking to reach an agreement through mediation, or are you already in a serious custody dispute where court proceedings may be necessary?**

## How to verify accredited mediation

The Australian Government's [Family Dispute Resolution Register](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/family-dispute-resolution/find-family-dispute-resolution-practitioner) lets you check a practitioner's accreditation and search for private mediators near you. [www.ag.gov.au](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/family-dispute-resolution/find-family-dispute-resolution-practitioner?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.ag.gov.au](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/family-dispute-resolution/navigating-family-dispute-resolution?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

For parenting disputes, ask specifically about **Family Dispute Resolution Practitioner (FDRP) accreditation**\. General mediation accreditation alone is not the same thing.

In most cases, parents must make a genuine effort to resolve parenting issues through FDR before applying for parenting orders. An accredited practitioner can issue a section 60I certificate if the dispute remains unresolved or FDR is considered inappropriate. Exceptions can apply, including in cases involving family violence, child abuse or urgency. [www.ag.gov.au](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/family-dispute-resolution/section-60i-certificates-family-dispute-resolution?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.ag.gov.au](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/family-dispute-resolution?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## Questions to ask before choosing a firm

- How much of your practice involves contested parenting and children's matters?
- Who will personally handle my case, and what experience do they have with matters like mine?
- Do you have an **accredited FDR practitioner in-house**, or will I need to engage someone separately?
- Can you assist with mediation, parenting plans and legally enforceable consent orders?
- What are the initial consultation fee, hourly rates and likely upfront costs?
- If mediation fails, can you continue to represent me in court?

If family violence, coercive control or safety concerns are involved, mention this privately at the outset so the lawyer can assess whether mediation is appropriate and what protective arrangements may be needed.

## My recommendation

I'd start by contacting **Northside Family Law Centre and Barton Family Lawyers in Chermside**, then **ABA Family Lawyers and Best Wilson Buckley near North Lakes**\. Compare them on the experience of the actual solicitor who would handle your matter, their approach to resolving conflict and whether they can connect you with an accredited FDR practitioner.

One question that would help me narrow this down further: **Are you mainly looking to reach an agreement through mediation, or are you already in a serious custody dispute where court proceedings may be necessary?**
